items: A **recursive** method calls itself on a **smaller** version of the same problem.
Every recursive method needs a **base case** that returns without recursing, and every call must move toward it.
Missing or unreachable base cases produce **`StackOverflowError`**.
Work placed **before** the recursive call runs on the way down; work placed **after** runs on the way back up.
Recursion costs memory and time because every call allocates its own parameters and locals.
Choose by the shape of the problem: **iteration** for counting and traversal, **recursion** for nested and self-referential structures.
